newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds little changed post-tender.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds little changed post-tender.

text.p: Australian bond yields were little changed from their pre-lunchtime firmer levels after the today's A$900 million Treasury bond tender result was seen as average.
Although bids were fairly tight and both stocks on offer had been in demand, traders said the result failed to dazzle the market and the focus is now switching to supply in the U.S.
"It was an ordinary result and my own gut feeling is that we could see some selling pressure from here with plenty of stock floating around," one trader said.
At 2.20 p.m. (0320 GMT), the March 10-year bond futures contract was 92.565, a tad below the 92.570 before lunch.

The A$600 million of November 2006 stock, which is currently the 10-year benchmark, fetched an average yield of 7.396 percent compared with around 7.40/7.36 percent seen quoted when final bids went in at 12.45 p.m. (0145 GMT).
Accepted bids were in a three basis points range, which was seen as reasonable for a longer dated stock.
The A$300 million of January 2001 issue went off at an average yield of 6.812 percent compared with a pre-tender level of around 6.825/6.785 percent, and bids were in a tight one basis point range.
Today's supply brought fixed coupon issuance for the fiscal year so far to A$5.7 billion.

In last month's mid-year review the Treasury raised its forecast for T-bond issuance to A$8.0/A$9.0 billion for the 1996/97 year ending June 30, up A$2.0 billion from the projection made in the August budget last year.

Meanwhile, U.S. Treasuries face the first leg of the quarterly refunding auctions which sees US$17.75 billion of three-notes on offer. The market reaction to the sale will set the early tone for local bonds on Wednesday, traders added.
